author: vladimir_ea
content:
it looks consistently the same for the first slot of the epoch - this is due to the additional processing required for the epoch transition? 
I see 9 reorgs yesterday, all on epoch transitions (blocks after skipped slots: 25670691, 25670754, 25671742, 25672476, 25672666, 25673175, 25674293, 25676145, 25676176).

author: potuz
content:
Yes it's mostly about the extra computation. However that should be cached by clients and we suspect there's just still unoptimized paths here. This is the only reason we can't move attestation deadline to 2 seconds at the fork. 

Also in addition after <@703742742135570499> report on the topic. Terence found out that one of the major operators being reorged is because of the combination between timing games and min bid: they play timing games and request bids at the latest, but anyway end up producing locally and they broadcast then themselves. If their blocks have many blobs, they're more likely to be reorged. People should be smarter playing timing games or at least not use a min bid on the first slot if they're playing timing games
